title: White Bread, Special Formula, Added Fiber

content.title: About
content.content: White bread made with a special formula and added dietary fiber is a loaf produced from high‑grade wheat flour enriched with extra fiber to boost its nutritional value. The bread has a soft crumb, light crust, and a mild neutral flavor, suitable for eating plain or as a base for sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fiber in the bread improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.
The special formula keeps the loaf tender even with the higher fiber content.
White bread is traditionally a source of quick‑release carbs, but added fiber slows absorption.
The product is made without preservatives, making it more natural.
Bread is often used as a base for open‑face sandwiches and appetizers.

items.title: Supports Digestive Health
items.content: Dietary fiber helps maintain regular bowel movements and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lower Glycemic Impact
items.content: Added fiber slows glucose absorption, helping to moderate blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Increases Satiety
items.content: Fiber prolongs the feeling of fullness, which can aid in weight management.

items.title: Source of B‑Vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour provides thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mineral Content
items.content: The loaf contains iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, supporting blood and bone health.

items.title: Gluten Allergy
items.content: Bread made from wheat contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Glycemic Index Considerations
items.content: Despite the added fiber, the base is still white flour, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: The product may contain moderate salt; those limiting sodium should account for it in their overall diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bread works well toasted, as a sandwich base, alongside soups and salads, or crumbled into casseroles. It can also be used for open‑face toppings with vegetables and lean proteins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box. For longer storage, freeze it and thaw at room temperature before use.
